title: Punctual purity via the canonical closed-point Kummer class
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], finite Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], and the canonical Kummer class family of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. For a regular Noetherian scheme $W$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] on which $\ell$ is invertible and a point $w\in W$, put $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and $j_w=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{W,w}\twoheadrightarrow\kappa(w)):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$ [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Define $W$ to be punctually pure at $w$ if the canonical Kummer class map $A_{\kappa(w)}\to j_w^! A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$ is an isomorphism, and punctually pure if this holds for every point. Here the map is obtained by transposing the level-$n=1$, untensored supported Ext class through the derived closed direct-image/support adjunction [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]; the exact direct-image comparison and the fully faithful inclusion of $D^+$ in $D$ are canonical. Finite dimension, Noetherianity of $W_w$ and regularity of $j_w$ are witnesses needed to evaluate the published class, not additional hypotheses on regular Noetherian $W$.

source.place: Expose XVI Definitions 3.2.1 and 3.2.2, printed p.244; canonical class: XVI 2.3.1--2.3.2.

proof.text: Construction obligations for the local pair. Put $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], $R$ is Noetherian regular local. The finiteness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters] gives $d=\dim R\in\mathbb N$. The definition of regular local supplies $d$ generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathfrak m_R$; [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] says that this list is a regular sequence. Thus $j=\operatorname{Spec}(R\twoheadrightarrow k)$ is a regular closed immersion of codimension $d$: it is closed by the affine quotient criterion of [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its source has one point, at which the defining ideal is precisely $\mathfrak m_R=(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$. The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is Noetherian since its coordinate ring is Noetherian, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian since $k$ is a field. The unit $\ell^{-1}$ on $W$ maps to a unit in $R$, hence in $k$. These are exactly the hypotheses needed to evaluate the class-calculus node; none is a further hypothesis on $W$.

Coefficient and derived objects. Set $A=\mathbb F_\ell=\Lambda_1$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $M=A_Z$, and $K=A_T(d)[2d]$. Construct $A_T(d)$ by the tensor powers of the roots-of-unity sheaf in [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], then regard it as a degree-zero complex and apply the cohomological shift in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Both $M$ and $K$ are bounded below, as each has a single possible nonzero cohomology degree. We use the fixed functors $F=j_*^+$ and $G=j^{!,+}$ and fixed adjunction $F\dashv G$ of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]. In particular the target will be $G(K)=j^{!,+}(A_T(d)[2d])$; no tensor product is moved through $j^!$ in this construction.

Take the level-$1$ untensored supported class $\eta_{j,1}:A_Z\to j_1^!A_T(d)[2d]$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] for the pair $j:Z\hookrightarrow T$ (there $\Lambda_1=A$, $c=d$). Its supported direct-image form is its transpose under the $Rj_*\dashv j_1^!$ adjunction named in that statement (the compact-support right adjoint; for the closed immersion $j$ the compactification is $(\mathrm{id},j)$, so $Rj_!=Rj_*$): $b=\varepsilon'_{A_T(d)[2d]}\circ Rj_*(\eta_{j,1}):Rj_*A_Z\to A_T(d)[2d]$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, with $\varepsilon'$ that adjunction's counit. Exact closed direct image agrees canonically with $Rj_*$ by [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction], so its source is the inclusion of $F(M)$. Both endpoints are in $D^+$; the strictly full-subcategory definition in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] identifies their Hom set with the Hom set in $D$. Let $b^+:F(M)\to K$ be this same morphism under that identification. This specifies the supported class, including its Kummer normalization, rather than choosing an arbitrary element of the Hom set. Its independence of the regular generators is the explicit independence clause of the class-calculus statement.

source.place: XVI 2.3.1--2.3.2; level-1 supported class and its bounded-below realization

proof.text: Actual map and predicates. Let $u:\mathrm{id}\to GF$ be the unit of the fixed adjunction in [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]. Define $\alpha_{W,w}=G(b^+)\circ u_M:M\to G(K)$. This is exactly the adjunction transpose: by the triangle identities its image under $a\mapsto\varepsilon_K\circ F(a)$ is $b^+$. Use the fixed shift comparison of that definition to write the target as $j_w^!(A_{W_w}(d_w))[2d_w]$. Define $\operatorname{PunctuallyPureAt}_\ell(W,w)$ to be $\operatorname{IsIso}(\alpha_{W,w})$, and define $\operatorname{PunctuallyPure}_\ell(W)$ to be $\forall w\in W,\operatorname{PunctuallyPureAt}_\ell(W,w)$. All data are the spectrum, quotient, tensor power, fixed supported class and fixed adjunction above. The only non-definitional obligations are the named dimension/regular-sequence results and the named class/adjunction interfaces already cited. In particular, no choice from a bare existence assertion of a class or a functor enters the definition.
